Resolves #21642

🌿 After this, no webpack build waits in line behind another it shares nothing with.

`buildThreads.mjs` ran its webpack builds one after another: seven threads per environment, the longest step of `build-all`. Each thread writes only its own bundle, chunk folder and copies, and no config cleans its output folder, so the builds now run through `runSteps`, the pool #21647 gave `all.mjs`, which moves to `buildScripts/util/runSteps.mjs` for both scripts. `build-all` starts one `buildThreads` run for both environments, so its fourteen builds share that run's pool: at most four at a time on 18 cores, beside the ESM build and the docs parse, and the old sequence on a 4-core runner. The build id is still stamped only after every build succeeded.

Evidence: L3 (local A/B on the shared M5 Max: byte-identical output trees and alternating `build-all` timings at a 1-minute load of 21 to 28) → L3 required (AC-2). Residual: AC-2's under-30 s needs a machine quiet enough to read, and AC-3's `prepare --rehearse` runs on cut day; both are below.

## Deltas from ticket

- The handover named per-worker output isolation as a prerequisite. The configs show none is needed: worker builds write `chunks/<worker>/` and their own bundle, `main` adds `chunks/main/`, the Font Awesome copy and `DefaultConfig.mjs`, `appworker` adds `chunks/app/`, `src/MicroLoader.mjs` and the per-app folders, and no config cleans its output folder (intake on the ticket).
- `build-all`'s two thread steps, one per environment, became one `-e all` step (Evolution below).
- `build-all` passes `-t all` to that step (`c6b2025083`, Sophie's CLI note): it builds every thread, so its thread run asks no question. Before, `build-all-questions` (no `-n`) let each environment's child ask which threads to build. That was two questions one after the other on a 4-core host, and two at once on one terminal since #21647 on a many-core one. A per-thread choice stays in `npm run build-threads`.

## Test Evidence

- **A/B, one worktree, outside CI.** `dev`'s `all.mjs` and `buildThreads.mjs`, copied from `origin/dev`, run against the branch's, alternating three times with a fixed build id. The first run of each arm starts from removed output trees, which are hashed.
  - Outputs: `dist/development`, `dist/production`, `dist/esm` and `docs/output`, 17,059 files, none missing, none extra, none differing.
  - Timings (s): sequential 84.2, 41.7, 69.1 (median 69.1); parallel 46.1, 40.3, 44.5 (median 44.5). 18 cores, 1-minute load 21 to 28.
- **Independent timing on the M5 Max** (Sophie, an isolated checkout, `npm run build-all -- -l no`, one excluded warm-up, a fixed build id; [receipt](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21642#issuecomment-7072182614)):
  - at `c6b2025083`, this head: 24.45, 22.29, 23.55 s, median **23.55 s**, at one-minute loads of 13.6 to 20.8;
  - at `f509e58836`, before `-t all`: 27.24, 33.61, 25.87 s, median 27.24 s, at loads of 12.5 to 23.9.
  - Both: 17,059 output files, and all 645 `neo-config.json` files carry the fixed id.
- `agent-preflight`: not hosted here; the baseline jobs run.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] AC-2: `npm run build-all` on merged `dev`, on the M5 Max, finishes under 30 s, median of three with the load recorded. Owner: Vega; the receipt goes on #21642.
- [ ] AC-3: `publish.mjs prepare --rehearse` reports every gate ✅ on the cut candidate. Owner: Vega, on cut day; the receipt goes on #21033 (its AC-3) and is linked from #21642.

## Evolution

The first shape kept `build-all`'s two thread steps, each `buildThreads` with its own pool: up to eight webpack builds beside the ESM build and the docs parse. Its A/B was byte-identical too, but at load 15 to 26 its median was worse (47.3 against 38.6 s). One run with one pool keeps the concurrency near #21647's bound and still lets the long environment split.
